intro: You've searched for a building surveyor near you, probably because you're buying a property, dealing with a problem in your current home, or planning work on a building. You want someone local who can assess the building and give you clear advice. We can introduce you to a suitable UK building surveyor who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a building surveyor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a building surveyor near them have a specific building concern and want expert advice from someone who can visit the property.
needs: You are buying an older or altered property and want to understand its condition before you commit.
You have noticed cracks, damp or other defects and need to know what is causing them and what to do next.
You are planning repairs or refurbishment and need help designing the work and managing the project.
You need advice on building regulations or compliance for a project you are about to start.
You are dealing with a dilapidations claim at the end of a lease and need a surveyor who understands the process.
context_heading: What to understand about finding a building surveyor near you
context: Many building surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process. Chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS after their name. Some specialist roles have their own bodies, such as the Faculty of Party Wall Surveyors or the Property Care Association for damp and timber specialists.

When you contact a surveyor, check the RICS directory, ask which report type you are getting and confirm whether the surveyor is independent of the sale. If asbestos is a concern, look for organisations accredited by UKAS for surveying. A local surveyor will be familiar with the typical building styles and issues in your area.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: The property address and the type of building, such as a house, flat or commercial premises.
Why you need a surveyor, for example a home purchase, a defect investigation or project management.
Any specific concerns you have, such as damp, cracks, roof problems or asbestos.
The age of the building and whether it has been altered or extended.
Whether you are buying, selling, leasing or already own the property.
Any deadlines you are working towards, such as a exchange date or lease end.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the building surveyor
questions: Are you a member of RICS, and what is your membership level?
Which type of survey report will you provide, and what does it cover?
Are you independent of the sale, and do you have any connection to the seller or agent?
Do you have experience with older or altered buildings like mine?
Can you advise on dilapidations, and have you handled similar cases?
What is the process if I have a complaint about your service?

faqs.q: How do I find a building surveyor near me?
faqs.a: You can search the RICS directory for chartered surveyors in your area, or ask iComply to introduce you to a suitable professional. A local surveyor will know the area and typical building issues.

faqs.q: What does a building surveyor do?
faqs.a: Building surveyors assess building condition, design and manage repairs and refurbishments, and advise on defects and regulations. They can help with home purchases, project management and dilapidations.

faqs.q: Do I need a building surveyor or a structural engineer?
faqs.a: A building surveyor can assess the overall condition of a property and advise on defects, while a structural engineer focuses on the structural integrity. For most home purchases, a building surveyor is the usual first step.

faqs.q: How much does a building surveyor cost?
faqs.a: Costs vary depending on the type of survey, the property size and location. The surveyor will quote you directly, so you can compare quotes and ask what is included.
